products.short_description: A user enrolls an iPhone or iPad into Intune and hits "Access Denied — you are not authorized to view this page" with an Activity Id and Session Id. It’s not the device — it’s a tenant-side authorization gate (license, MDM scope, enrollment restriction, or Conditional Access). This guide turns the on-screen IDs into the exact root cause and a scoped fix, with five PowerShell tools.
products.description:
The iPhone says "Access Denied." The cause is in your tenant — and the IDs on the screen point straight to it.

A user starts Device Management enrollment into Microsoft Intune and lands on "Access Denied — You are not authorized to view this page. Your IT department may be able to help," with a block of Diagnostic information for IT (Activity Id, Session Id, Timestamp). Enrollment stops and the device stays unmanaged. This is not a device fault — it’s the Intune enrollment authorization service refusing the sign-in because a tenant-side gate blocks it.

Deterministic diagnosis — not trial-and-error

The Session Id and Activity Id on the screen are correlation identifiers. You look them up in the Entra sign-in logs; the failed enrollment sign-in’s failure reason and its Conditional Access tab name the exact gate. This guide takes you from those IDs to the cause in about two minutes.

Every common gate, in the order it happens

  • Licensing — the user has no enabled Intune service plan (the most common cause).
  • MDM user scope — the user is outside the Microsoft Intune MDM scope in Entra ’s Mobility (MDM and WIP) settings.
  • Enrollment restrictions — iOS/iPadOS or personally-owned devices are blocked, or the user has hit their device limit.
  • Conditional Access — a policy blocks the enrollment sign-in, or requires a compliant device the not-yet-enrolled device can’t be (the classic chicken-and-egg).
  • Account — a guest/B2B or disabled account.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, proven

Self-guided, click-by-click documentation plus five PowerShell tools, and a clear engineer-session narrative.

  • Simpler — capture the IDs, read the failed sign-in, confirm the gate, fix it, re-enroll.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open-ended support engagement.
  • Tested — Capture → Read the sign-in → Confirm the gate → Remediate → Re-enroll & validate → Prevent, with evidence at each step.

What’s inside

  • Solution Overview, Requirements, the Root-Cause & Remediation Guide (Phase 1–4), Testing, Troubleshooting/FAQ, and Best Practices — every object named, with a GCC High note.
  • Five PowerShell tools: Get-EnrollmentSignin (the failed enrollment sign-in + CA result), Get-UserIntuneLicense, Get-MdmUserScope, Get-EnrollmentRestrictions, and Get-EnrollmentCA — each turns a gate into a yes/no answer.

The repeatable way

One fixed price — keep the runbook and scripts and re-run them for the next "Access Denied" enrollment, and fix the class problem so the next user doesn’t hit the same wall.

The bottom line

A two-minute root cause from the on-screen IDs, a surgical fix that doesn’t weaken your other controls, the device enrolled and managed, and evidence for the ticket. Downloadable guide plus scripts.
